2 03-11-2025 Heard the parties.

2. The petitioners are named in the F.I.R. and apprehending their arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 222 of 2010 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 448, 323,
504, 376, 379, 380, 436, 500 of the IPC and Section 27 of Arms Act.
3. The allegation against petitioners is to commit rape upon victim/ informant while she went to attend natural call.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.73994 of 2025(2) dt.03-11-2025 4.

It is submitted by Mr. Ramakant Sharma learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners that from the perusal of FIR itself it can be gathered that the present case was lodged Lal Jha vs The State Of Bihar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196591337/
1 falsely against petitioners in the background of the dispute arising out of removal of the wooden stall of the husband of the victim/ informant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that during said occurrence the petitioner side received serious injuries for which cousin sister of the petitioner namely, Sudhira Devi registered police case on the same date i.e., on 18.01.2006 against husband of the informant and family members which was registered as Phulparas P.S. Case No. 13 of 2006 and just to counter said case the present false case was lodged on same date.

5. Arguing further, Mr. Sharma submitted that taking note of all such aspects after investigation police submitted final form in present case through charge-sheet no. 182 of 2009 dated 19.10.2009,
whereafter protest cum complaint was filed, on which, after inquiry the learned trial court took cognizance for the alleged offences against petitioners.

It is submitted that the petitioners preferred Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.73994 of 2025(2) dt.03-11-2025 revision against the cognizance order, which was set aside by learned Sessions Judge, Madhubani despite the same learned trial court took cognizance for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC against petitioners.

6. Arguing further, it is submitted that even in the complaint case during inquiry the occurrence was supported by the family members of the victim/ informant who are the accused of Phulparas P.S.
Case No. 13 of 2006.
7.

Explaining criminal antecedents of the petitioners, it is submitted by Mr. Sharma that petitioner no. 1 was accused in two cases, where he has already been acquitted, whereas petitioner no. 2 found involved in 4 more criminal cases where he is on bail in three cases and acquitted in fourth case i.e.,
G.R. Case No. 237 of 2025, the details of which is available in para no. 3 of the bail petition.
It is pointed out that none of these cases are of similar nature.

It is pointed out that if the merit of this case otherwise convincing in favor of petitioners merely on the basis of criminal antecedents ordinarily the bail prayer of the petitioners should not be declined.

In support of his Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.73994 of 2025(2) dt.03-11-2025 submission Mr. Sharma relied upon the legal report of Hon'ble Supreme Court as available through Prabhakar Tewari vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr. reported in (2020) 11 SCC 648.
8.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr. reported in (2020) 11 SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned APP while opposing prayer of bail submitted that considering the statement of inquiry witnesses the learned trial court found this case prima-facie correct against petitioners and therefore took cognizance, where specifically allegation was raised against both of these petitioners.

9. In view of aforesaid factual and legal submission and by taking note of fact that the police after investigation submitted final form against these petitioners and did not sent up them for facing trial,
coupled with the fact that prima-facie allegation was raised immediately after lodging case against husband of the informant/ victim as discussed aforesaid, accordingly both above-named petitioners,
in the event of their arrest or surrender before the court below within a period of four weeks, are directed to be released on bail, furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.73994 of 2025(2) dt.03-11-2025 each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned JM 1st Class, Jhanjharpur, Madhubani /concerned Court,
where the case is pending in connection with Complaint Case No. 222 of 2010, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C/Section 482(2) of BNSS.

Before parting order, it would be apposite to mention that during course of argument Mr.
Sharma drawn attention of this Court that order of Anticipatory Bail which is the impugned order was passed by learned trial court on 02.02.2023 itself, but despite of repeated application on several occasions, the certified copy could obtained only on 01.09.2025.
11.

Considering the submission, let a copy of this order be send to learned District Judge,
Madhubani to take appropriate actions in administrative side against the persons who are in affairs of issuing certify copy at Jhanjharpur.
